Okay, so I'm trying to figure out which option serves as protective barriers along coastlines and is often destroyed by strong hurricanes. The options are A) erosion of land, B) buildup of dunes, C) new buildings, D) buildup from oil rigs.

First, I remember that coastal areas often have natural barriers like sand dunes to protect against storms. I think dunes are built up over time, so option B seems likely. But I'm not 100% sure.

I recall that during hurricanes, the dunes can be eroded or even destroyed. For example, after a hurricane, the sand might get washed away, leaving the coastline more vulnerable. That makes sense because without the dunes, the storm surge can come inland easier.

Looking at the options, erosion of land (A) doesn't really act as a barrier. It's more about the land being worn away, which isn't protective. New buildings (C) might be constructed, but they aren't natural barriers and can be destroyed themselves. Buildup from oil rigs (D) seems unrelated to natural protection.

So, putting it all together, the correct answer is B) the buildup of dunes along the coast over time because they provide protection that can be destroyed by strong hurricanes.
